blocks.markdown: [Draft PR 7]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]) is open, unmerged and verified at `ffc5241a`: bounded native/browser expressions, FP-safe typed persistence and the self-contained verifier, now including the corrected Python guarded-batch codec and pre-transaction request snapshots. The full clean-export verifier and independent correctness/reentry reviews pass. Post-fix timings show partial recovery but residual cost, so fresh FP/codec research is active and item 2 is not accepted. Accepted item-1 source stays at `e42a8adc`; exact final v1 remains preserved at `fcc3e71f`. [Raw correctness/performance evidence]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]) and the [selected renewed research decision]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]) were verified on main before this fix. Original/frozen source and deployed private v1 Site remain unchanged.

**Iteration 1 is accepted within its bounded four-type contract. Iteration 2 remains held after a partial performance recovery; iterations 3–10 stay queued in order.** Native/browser/store correctness, independent reviews, migration, 115 isolated batch/request children and the full 267-source clean-export normal/direct-sanitizer verifier pass on published source `ffc5241a`. Counts overlap, not a certification score. The earlier corrected native SQL study (42 pairs/12 workloads, median ratios 0.969–1.049×) has no declared primary signal; all 95% intervals include 1 and modest regressions remain possible. The original distinct persisted float256 study measured 26–27% median cost (~3.5→4.2–4.4 ms), with all 480 exact outcomes; it remains preserved, not replaced. After researched batch conversion, two ordered studies each use 42 fresh-process pairs/two rounds/14 controls on the same closed 320-fact/10-commit history. All 168 processes/11,760 public outcomes pass, with recorded exits/provenance/schedule and all 1,176 pair records/statistics independently reverified. Against hardened8b with the SAME native artifact, float256 improves ~11% (ratios 0.890/0.887) and wide output ~24% (0.757/0.762). Against accepted item1, float256 still costs ~5.6%/8.5% and wide output ~12%; tiny/empty controls also retain investigation signals. Wide means 256 rows ×8 cells/1,024 float cells, not 1,024 stored facts. Thus full recovery and item-2 acceptance are NOT claimed. Profiles show constant 6/7 fresh FP reads per query/query_json across shapes, without skipping per-cell validation; counts are not exclusive causation. Original analyzer acceptance omissions are retained and closed for these recorded runs by separate fail-closed checks, not rewritten results. The timed Python assignment can include previous-result disposal; intervals are descriptive per-control, not family-wise or universal guarantees. Fresh parallel primary-source FP-observer and codec/vectorization research is reopened before any further patch. [Durable correctness/negative-candidate checkpoint]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]) and prior raw/research archives remain intact; [all new raw timings/independent closures]([PRIVATE_REFERENCE_REMOVED]) are now verified in main checkpoint `4c6c79cc`. The first candidate's close/subtype defects, original diagnostics and incomplete large Python-carrier sanitizer transport remain retained, not relabeled passes. For item 1, initial 23–36% isolated losses did not reproduce in 756 CPU-pinned A/B pairs (paired medians ~0.97–1.03×); both datasets are preserved. Production readiness is not claimed.
